summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman was admitted due to confusion, tremor, double vision, and nausea following a recent hospital discharge, where her phenytoin dose had been increased. Her phenytoin level was found to be supratherapeutic at 22.2, consistent with toxicity, likely exacerbated by improved absorption from reduced bowel edema after diuresis and interactions with warfarin. She was evaluated by neurology, transitioned from phenytoin to levetiracetam (Keppra), and monitored with EEG, which showed no seizure activity. Symptoms gradually improved over the admission. Her INR was subtherapeutic at 1.9, prompting an increase in warfarin from 5 mg to 8 mg daily, with INR stabilizing at 2.1 by discharge. She received supportive care for chronic conditions including heart failure, fibromyalgia, and hypokalemia. Physical therapy confirmed safe ambulation. She was discharged home with home services, medication changes, and follow-up plans.
problems: Chronic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
